intro: Step into Cumalıkızık, a historic town in Bursa province whose story begins in the 14th century. This is a foundation village from the Ottomans' first century, lived in on the same plan for seven hundred years. Its cobbled lanes and overhanging houses are still intact.
history: In the Ottomans' first century, Cumalıkızık was one of the endowment villages that fed Bursa. Because its income was tied to a foundation, it was never broken up — and that is the secret of what you see. Of its roughly 270 houses, more than half still stand. Look up: their three storeys of timber-laced mudbrick almost meet overhead across the lanes. The street pattern and plot divisions have not changed since the fourteenth century.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the village square, the bay-windowed houses, the Zekiye Hatun Mosque, the Ethnography Museum and, beneath your feet, the cobbled lanes.
facts: Did you know? The village was inscribed by UNESCO not on its own but together with Bursa's monuments, under the title 'Bursa and Cumalıkızık: the Birth of the Ottoman Empire'. Because its income was tied to a foundation, it was never broken up, so its street pattern and plot divisions are unchanged since the fourteenth century. More than half of its roughly 270 houses still stand, and people still live in them: this is a working village, not a museum.
outro: This brings our tour of Cumalıkızık to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Remember that these are people's homes, and enjoy your visit.
